newsitem.title: USA: Chicago school board OKs $500 mln of bonds.
newsitem.headline: Chicago school board OKs $500 mln of bonds.

text.p: The Chicago School Reform Board of Trustees late Wednesday approved the issuance of up to $500 million of alternate bonds backed by the school system's general obligation pledge.
Kenneth Gotsch, the school system's chief fiscal officer, said proceeds from the bonds will continue a capital improvement program adopted in January 1996.

Gotsch said $350 million to $400 million of the bonds, which will be paid off with personal property tax replacement revenues, may be sold in mid-April with Goldman, Sachs & Co. as the senior manager and BA Securities as the co-senior manager.
While MBIA Insurance Corp. has reserved capacity for the bond issue, Gotsch said he felt the schools' credit was "sufficiently strong" to try to attract better insurance bids for the deal.
MBIA had insured $350 million of bonds sold by the school board last April.
The remainder of the $500 million of bonds authorized Wednesday would probably be sold next year, according to Gotsch.
Meanwhile, the school board is weighing options for selling another $600 million of bonds to bring capital improvement spending to $1.4 billion.

Gotsch said one option is tapping unused bonding authority of the now-dormant Chicago School Finance Authority, which up until 1995 had oversight powers over the schools' finances. A 1995 state of Illinois law turned control of the schools over to Chicago Mayor Richard Daley and mothballed the finance authority.

A second option is raising the property tax levy within the state-imposed property tax cap that limits growth of annual property tax revenues to five percent or the rate of inflation, whichever is less. Gotsch said that if approved by the school board, a levy increase could generate an additional $30 million to $40 million a year.
A third option rests with a bill pending in the Illinois Senate that would authorize the state to issue $1 billion of GO bonds for primary and secondary public schools.
